MC	<p>a193_bf39</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a74;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a74;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a74;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, atw, +++, atw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1bb8_b023</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dex, +++, dex"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8574_3ddf</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6f5c0c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>4fa9_b12d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #246d4c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekn, +++, ekn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b663_f4b2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aew, +++, aew"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>25eb_9ee8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>f25b_cb46</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8e4815;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cnr, +++, cnr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9ffe_aa03</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8e4815;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hkt, +++, hkt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e107_887d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8e4815;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dmw, +++, dmw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, amw, +++, amw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8e4815;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e3da_0936</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a74;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a74;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a74;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kpr, +++, kpr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>11f4_8aa4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6f5c0c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhp, +++, bhp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6424_eabc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #246d4c;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9f2d52;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bkt, +++, bkt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>aa1c_ccc0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9f2d52;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dry, +++, dry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>fee0_d57b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, efp, +++, efp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f8ce_da74</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>5660_333b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4158a9;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cpt, +++, cpt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7552_68da</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene K</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4158a9;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ktx, +++, ktx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5185_fb6a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6f5c0c;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, enp, +++, enp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>815b_2498</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4158a9;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f2d52;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cmw, +++, cmw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ed96_1287</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8e4815;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mpx, +++, mpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>491f_46f9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6f5c0c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hjk, +++, hjk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a12f_8cdf</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4158a9;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f2d52;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdf, +++, bdf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c5e4_cf97</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, rtx, +++, rtx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #246d4c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #4158a9;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f2d52;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>3dc0_49ff</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a74;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a74;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a74;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fmt, +++, fmt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2af5_050b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cnx, +++, cnx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2063_0f9f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8e4815;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a74;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a74;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a74;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene Y</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bwy, +++, bwy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a5fa_520d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6f5c0c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene K</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #4158a9;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cjk, +++, cjk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>46fe_8585</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #8e4815;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cky, +++, cky"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9342_c26f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bce, +++, bce"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8fd0_5e09</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #4158a9;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #4158a9;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dhy, +++, dhy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>84f9_a477</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6f5c0c;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fmw, +++, fmw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ftx, +++, ftx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ee8c_db50</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6f5c0c;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9f2d52;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aew, +++, aew"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #8e4815;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8e4815;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bcf, +++, bcf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>b906_499e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #246d4c;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, etw, +++, etw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5319_5915</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #026787;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #026787;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #026787;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f2d52;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fhk, +++, fhk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #246d4c;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bnw, +++, bnw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>eae8_0d55</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d3729;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d3729;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abf, +++, abf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>1085_93ac</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a74;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006a74;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a74;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #8f3779;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3779;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afn, +++, afn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d2ab_660c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #336e22;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #336e22;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #336e22;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #2f6191;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #2f6191;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9f2d52;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9f2d52;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fwx, +++, fwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
