MC	<p>ed18_72cb</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #5a6500;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5a6500;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a74;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a74;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a74;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdt, +++, cdt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>24c7_ae95</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #246d4c;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #246d4c;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hjt, +++, hjt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7529_157f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #815300;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815300;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d62;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d62;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d62;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7f3a9e;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7f3a9e;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, afm, +++, afm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0c3d_4cad</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6f5c0c;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6f5c0c;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a74;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006a74;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a74;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6249af;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6249af;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6249af;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, chy, +++, chy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
